summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with a history of end-stage renal disease, diastolic heart failure, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, and atrial fibrillation was admitted after developing chest pain and hypotension during a dialysis session. Her symptoms were brief, without diaphoresis or ECG changes, and cardiac enzymes remained negative, ruling out myocardial infarction. Hypotension was attributed to excessive fluid removal during dialysis, leading to demand ischemia. She received a fluid bolus, which stabilized her blood pressure. Nephrology consultation recommended a dry weight of 53 kg and temporary discontinuation of antihypertensive medications until reassessment at the next dialysis session. Her rhythm was managed with continued amiodarone and anticoagulation. Chest X-ray showed no acute abnormalities with interval improvement, and blood cultures were negative. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to hold certain blood pressure medications, resume others based on dialysis team guidance, and take amiodarone daily, along with close follow-up.
